subject: Keep the setup wizard closed when a configured database is unreachable (#6333)
message:
Keep the setup wizard closed when a configured database is unreachable (#6333)

* Keep the setup wizard closed when a configured database is unreachable

DatabaseDetective.isDatabaseEmpty caught any connection failure and
reported the database as empty. Both callers, Listener startup and
InitializationFilter, use that result to decide whether to present the
unauthenticated setup wizard, so a database-connectivity failure on an
already-configured deployment reopened the wizard, exposing the stored
database credentials in the rendered form and letting an unauthenticated
user reconfigure and persist their own settings.

Only a genuinely unconfigured instance (no connection URL) is now treated
as empty on a connection failure; a configured instance that cannot be
reached is reported as not empty, so it fails startup with a connection
error instead of reopening setup. Also stop the finally block from
returning inside a close() failure, which could otherwise flip a
non-empty result to empty.

Adds a regression test that a configured but unreachable database is not
reported as empty.

### Summary
`DatabaseDetective.isDatabaseEmpty(Properties)` treated any exception while connecting as "the database is empty" (`catch (Exception e) { return true; }`). Both callers, `Listener` at startup and `InitializationFilter`, use that to decide whether to show the unauthenticated setup wizard. So on an already-configured deployment, a database-connectivity failure at startup (a DB outage or restart) made the instance report itself empty and **reopen the unauthenticated setup wizard**, which renders the stored DB credentials and lets an unauthenticated user reconfigure the instance and persist their own settings back to `openmrs-runtime.properties`.

### Change
On a connection failure, only treat the instance as empty when it is genuinely unconfigured (no `connection.url`). A configured instance that cannot be reached is reported as not empty, so startup fails with a connection error instead of reopening setup. Unconfigured/fresh installs (null or empty properties) still return empty, so the normal first-run wizard is unaffected. Also removed the `return true` inside the `finally` block's `close()` handler, which could otherwise override a non-empty result.

### Tests
`DatabaseDetectiveTest.shouldNotReportConfiguredButUnreachableDatabaseAsEmpty`: a configured instance whose database is unreachable is not reported as empty. The existing null-properties and empty-properties cases (still empty) continue to pass.

Addresses GHSA-jqhq-p753-2hwj. This is the reopen root cause;

subject: (fix) Pass the browserslist targets to the app shell's CSS minimizer (#1885)
message:
(fix) Pass the browserslist targets to the app shell's CSS minimizer (#1885)

* (fix) Pass the browserslist targets to the app shell's CSS minimizer

The app shell's rspack config never set optimization.minimizer, so production builds used rspack's default Lightning CSS minimizer with its own browser targets. Those targets are old enough that Lightning CSS downlevels every logical property in the shell's CSS, including all of Carbon, into physical properties guarded by :lang() language lists, repeated for :-webkit-any and :-moz-any, plus mirrored rules for RTL languages. On main that is 6,594 fallback rules and about two thirds of 3 MB of CSS.

The shared rspack and webpack configs for modules already pass browserslist-config-openmrs to their CSS minimizers. This does the same for the shell, reusing the browserTargets the config already passes to swc. Setting minimizer replaces rspack's default pair, so the JS minimizer is listed alongside it.

The styleguide stylesheet is excluded from the minimizer. The config compiles it with sass, names it after a hash of that output and copies it in as a static file, so minifying it afterwards changed its bytes under a name that no longer matched them. Sass already emits it compressed; leaving it alone costs about 3 KB gzipped and keeps the name honest.

Built from the same commit before and after: shell CSS goes from 3.03 MB to 1.11 MB raw in total and the main stylesheet from 163 KB to 104 KB gzipped, with no fallback rules left. JS output is byte-identical; only the entry file's hash changes because it embeds the renamed CSS chunk names.

* Mark the copied styleguide stylesheet as minified instead of excluding it by name

The exclude regex encoded the 16-character hash length used to name the
file, so the two had to move together and nothing checked that they did.
Setting info.minimized on the copy pattern tells the CSS minimizer the
asset is already minified, whatever it is called. Output is unchanged.

* chore: Remove redundant styleguide copy comment

Remove the explanatory comment above the styleguide copy pattern following review feedback. Keep the minimized asset metadata unchanged.

description:
Background

prTitle: (feat) Federate most of the Module Federation runtime
summary: Stop shipping the Module Federation runtime once per remote (~67 kB per app entry)
description:
Background
Every frontend module's remote entry currently embeds its own copy of the Module Federation runtime (@module-federation/runtime-core + sdk, ~67 kB of each ~85 kB entry). Measured on the reference application, MF machinery totals 456 kB on the login page and 607 kB on the home page — 11–13% of all JavaScript fetched. The genuinely per-app portion (container module map + share-scope metadata) is only ~15–18 kB; the runtime itself is identical across remotes and should ship once.
Requested change
Investigate and enable federation-runtime hoisting/sharing in the shared rspack config (e.g. the ModuleFederation runtime experiments/options in current rspack / module-federation releases) so the runtime is provided once (by the app shell) and remotes reference it, rather than each embedding a copy. Apply the equivalent in the shared webpack config, or document the divergence if webpack has no equivalent mechanism.
Acceptance criteria
Remote entry size reduction measured and recorded on a representative assembled distribution (expected: roughly 67 kB per remote entry).

A page load fetches the federation runtime once, not once per app (verify via network trace / source-map attribution).

Remotes built with the previous tooling still load correctly alongside new ones (mixed-version distribution verified).

Build-level test or CI check in the tooling package guarding against the runtime reappearing in remote entries.

summary: Include obs uuid in the obstree response
description:
The obstree resource (the ObsTreeResource class in the REST module) serializes each observation as value, obsDatetime, interpretation, and reference range fields, but not the obs uuid.
This means clients cannot distinguish:
the same observation appearing in multiple branches of the tree (for example when configured root concept sets overlap, such as Bloodwork containing Hematology), versus

two genuinely distinct observations that happen to share the same value and datetime (for example one result per order, entered against the same encounter).

The patient chart's test results viewer currently has to de-duplicate using an obsDatetime plus value heuristic, which cannot tell those two cases apart. See https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart/pull/3374 for the frontend side and the full investigation.
Proposed change: add the obs uuid to the observation map built by the resource, alongside value and obsDatetime. This is additive and backwards compatible. Existing consumers ignore the extra field, and the frontend can switch its de-duplication identity to the uuid when present, falling back to the heuristic for older servers.

subject: (fix) Don't label naturally expired medications as Discontinued (#3337)
message:
(fix) Don't label naturally expired medications as Discontinued (#3337)

(fix) Stop labeling auto-expired medications as Discontinued in the visits panel

The medications summary in the visit detail overview tagged any order
with `autoExpireDate <= now` as "Discontinued", conflating two distinct
states: clinician-initiated discontinuation (dateStopped set) and
natural completion of a duration-bound course (autoExpireDate reached).
OpenMRS core treats these as separate predicates (Order#isDiscontinued
vs Order#isExpired), and the medications detail table elsewhere in this
codebase already gates the "Discontinued" tag on dateStopped alone --
this view was the outlier.

The helper is renamed `isPastMedication` -> `isDiscontinued` to match
the tag it gates, the `autoExpireDate` branch is removed, and the
comparison switches to strict `<`. This matches core's
`checkDate.after(dateStopped)` semantics, and means a future-scheduled
dateStopped no longer pre-emptively shows the tag.

The previous `action === 'DISCONTINUE'` branch is also dropped: a
discontinuation order is a separate row pointing at the original via
previousOrder; the original is the one whose dateStopped gets set.
Tagging the discontinuation order itself "Discontinued" was labeling
the wrong row.

Whether to surface a separate "Completed"/"Expired" tag for naturally
ended orders is left to a follow-up.

summary: Allow expression identifiers that start with a digit in esm-expression-evaluator
description:
Background
Form field ids are free-form: the form builder only enforces uniqueness, so ids like 1stVisit are allowed. The expression evaluator's parser (jsep) rejects these with "Variable names cannot start with a number", so no form expression can refer to such a field by name. Authors have to use useFieldValue('1stVisit') instead. The form engine's old eval-based post-submission helper accepted these ids by substituting text, so some saved forms may rely on them.
Rewriting expressions with a regex before parsing was tried in openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib#843 and abandoned. It has to replicate jsep's lexer, it silently changed the contents of regex literals, and it was flagged for polynomial ReDoS. This should be handled by the evaluator's own parser.
Requested change
Teach the evaluator's jsep instance to read a word that starts with a digit but isn't a numeric literal (e.g. 1stVisit) as an identifier. This can be done with a gobble-token hook registered ahead of @jsep-plugin/numbers. The hook reads the run of identifier characters, and if that isn't a valid number, emits an Identifier and chains member access and calls via gobbleTokenProperty(). Because jsep only calls the hook at token boundaries, the contents of string, template and regex literals are unaffected.
A prototype against jsep 1.4.0 and the evaluator's current plugins works for all of the cases below. The behavior can be always-on or opt-in through a compile() option.

compile, evaluate and ex

message:
(fix) Don't crash the registration form when address hierarchy levels aren't JSON (#2756)

The addresshierarchy module's `getOrderedAddressHierarchyLevels.form` endpoint
content-negotiates: with a browser-style `Accept` header it can answer with a
200 response carrying an OpenMRS HTML page instead of the expected JSON array.
`openmrsFetch` parses the body in a try / catch, so that response resolves as a
success with `data` left `undefined`, and no error is set.

`useOrderedAddressHierarchyLevels` then derived `orderedFields` with no
fallback, so `AddressComponent` ran `orderedFields.map(...)` on `undefined` and
threw during render, white-screening the whole registration form.

Give the derived arrays a fallback and validate the response body in a shared
fetcher, so a body that isn't the expected array is reported through SWR's
`error` instead of masquerading as an empty result. The address field
component's existing `errorFetchingFieldOrder` guard then renders its error
notification rather than an address section with no fields.

message:
(feat) Improve no active visit empty state in admission workspace (#2172)

* feat: improve no active visit admission state

Show a start visit prompt when a patient without an active visit is selected for admission.

Add scoped workspace styles and test coverage for the no active visit admission workflow.

* Show admit and start visit buttons on ward admission patient search cards

Implements the design agreed in the PR review discussion: in the Add
patient to ward search, the patient card is no longer clickable. Patients
with an active visit get an enabled Admit button that opens the admission
workspace. Patients without one get a start visit button next to a
disabled Admit button, which enables in place once the visit is saved.

The patient search workspace gains an optional selectPatientButton prop
so the ward can configure the button without leaking it into the other
consumers of the search workspace (appointments, patient lists, queues).

* Pass the patient to the start visit button slot on search result cards

The banner rendered start-visit-button-slot2 without the patient in the
slot state, so the start visit button launched the visit form with an
undefined patient prop. The visit form and the extensions it hosts, like
the billing check-in form, dereference that patient, which surfaced as
requests to patient/undefined and post-save callback failures on billing
enabled instances.

* Give the admit patient workspace a footer and visit context

The workspace rendered its primary action as a ghost link floating in an
otherwise empty panel, with a back link of equal visual weight beneath it
and no information beyond the patient banner. The admit and back actions
now sit in the standard workspace footer button bar, matching the bed
selection form, and the body shows the active visit's type, location,
and start time alongside the existing admission warnings.

AdmitPatientButton accepts optional kind and size props so the footer can
render it as a primary action without changing its ghost styling in the
admission requests bench.

* Auto-open the admission workspace after starting a visit

After the visit form saves in the Add patient to ward flow, the admission
workspace now opens automatically for the same patient instead of
returning the user to the search results to click Admit. The callback
flows from the ward's workspace props through the patient search context
and banner into the visit form's onVisitStarted hook.

Launching a child workspace immediately after another closes previously
tripped a lifecycle race in workspace2 that could mount the closed form's
component with the new workspace's props. That race was fixed in
openmrs/openmrs-esm-core#1807, which is included in the framework build
this branch resolves after rebasing onto main. Verified locally against
that build: repeated start-visit-then-admit flows land on the admission
workspace with no stale component mount and no patient/undefined
requests.

* Use flex instead of hard-coded button widths in admission workspace footer

Carbon's .cds--btn-set .cds--btn rule caps footer buttons at 196px and
out-specifies a single CSS module class, which is why the previous rule
needed !important. Doubling the class wins on specificity instead, and
flex: 1 splits the row evenly without hard-coding a 50% width. With two
buttons the layout is unchanged; in the error state the lone back button
now fills the footer instead of stopping at half width.

Addresses review feedback from @ibacher.

subject: (fix) Patient search should bypass service worker caching (#2638)
message: (fix) Patient search should bypass service worker caching (#2638)
prTitle: (fix) Patient search should bypass service worker caching
summary: Service worker rescans the entire dynamic-route registration table (IndexedDB) on every GET request
description:
Background
The OMRS service worker's default request handler (esm-app-shell/src/service-worker/routing.ts) determines the caching strategy for every GET request. When a request carries no x-omrs-offline-caching-strategy header, it falls back to getHandlerKeyFromDynamicRouteRegistrations, which on every request:
opens a fresh ServiceWorkerDb (Dexie/IndexedDB) connection,

reads the entire dynamicRouteRegistrations table via .toArray(), and

compiles and tests a fresh new RegExp(route.pattern) against the URL for every registration.

This cost is negligible when the table is empty, but the table grows once offline mode is enabled and patients are synced — each synced patient (and its clinical data) registers dynamic routes. As a result, every un-headered GET — including live patient search and each paginated page — pays an IndexedDB open + full table scan + N regex compilations before the request is even dispatched. This is client-side overhead unrelated to network reachability, so it degrades performance even when the backend is on a fast LAN.
Requested change
Reduce the per-request cost of dynamic-route lookup in the service worker so it does not scale linearly with the number of registered offline routes on every request. Options include caching the registration list in memory (invalidated on registerDynamicRoute / clearDynamicRoutes messages), reusing a single ServiceWorkerDb/Dexie connection instead of constructing one per request, and precompiling the route regexes. prTitle: Fix render visit summary sections in configured order
summary: Patient Visit Summary Printing
description:
Add a configurable, pluggable visit summary PDF export to openmrs-module-patientdocuments. When a patient moves between facilities or visits a community health worker, clinicians can print a one-page structured summary of the visit.
Each section (vitals, diagnoses, allergies, etc.) activates based on an Initializer config key. Any external module can contribute its own section by implementing the VisitSummarySection interface, with no changes required to patientdocuments core.
Sections included:
Facility header + patient info

Vitals (configurable concept UUIDs)

Diagnoses, Conditions, Allergies

Medications, Lab Results, Visit Notes

## Summary

The visit summary PDF ignored each section's configured order. Section order is stored as `report.visitSummary.section.<key>.order` and the renderer already emits sections into the intermediate XML sorted by `getOrder()`, but `visitSummaryFopStylesheet.xsl` called each section's template from a hardcoded sequence, so the PDF always came out in that fixed order regardless of configuration. Enabling and disabling sections worked; reordering silently did nothing.

The root template now walks the XML in document order (`<xsl:apply-templates select="*"/>`), so the renderer's sort determines the PDF sequence. Each section's named template became a match template, which shortens its internal paths from document-root-relative to node-relative. Per-section output is unchanged. The footer is skipped in the body flow since it renders as `fo:static-content` on every page.

This surfaced now because the admin config page makes reordering possible for the first time.

No. With no order configured, each section's default order (facility header 100, patient info 200, vitals 300, diagnoses 400, conditions 450, lab results 475, allergies 500, medications 550, footer 900) produces the same sequence the hardcoded list did.
